lead: >-
  Lake Furnas in Minas Gerais can be visited on a 12-day motorcycle tour of Brazil. After São Paulo, Paraty, Rio de Janeiro and historic towns, the route reaches Capitólio, where a boat trip on the lake offers views of canyons and waterfalls. Discover how much time the itinerary allows here, how demanding the riding days are and which services are actually included.
---

## Tours visiting Lake Furnas: which itinerary should you choose?

[Lake Furnas](/brazil/place/lake-furnas/) is in the state of Minas Gerais near [Capitólio](/brazil/place/capitolio/). Its shoreline, canyons and waterfalls can be viewed by boat. For travelers, what matters is how the lake features in the journey: you could come just for a few hours on the water, or make Capitólio a stop on a longer journey through southeastern Brazil.

Our catalog features {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} passing through the lake area. One option is our [12-day motorcycle tour of Brazil](/brazil/tour/brazil-motorcycle-tour-12-days/). **Furnas is part of the main route**, with one day in Capitólio devoted specifically to a boat outing. This is quite different from tours that mention the lake only as a possible optional excursion.

You can read about the lake itself on the [Lake Furnas page](/brazil/place/lake-furnas/). Here, we focus on a specific trip combining the lake with cities, the Atlantic coastline and long motorcycle rides. Other regional combinations are available in our [Brazil tours catalog](/brazil/tour/).

## How the 12-day motorcycle route works

The journey starts and ends in São Paulo. From the city, the route heads to [Paraty](/brazil/place/paraty/) on the Costa Verde coast and then to [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/). After the urban and coastal stages, the route turns inland towards [Petrópolis](/brazil/place/petropolis/), [Tiradentes](/brazil/place/tiradentes/) and Capitólio.

| Stage | Itinerary |
|---|---|
| Days 1–2 | Arrival, São Paulo, collecting motorcycles |
| Days 3–5 | Costa Verde coast, Paraty and journey to Rio |
| Days 6–8 | Rio, Petrópolis, road towards Tiradentes |
| Day 9 | Tiradentes and arrival near Lake Furnas |
| Day 10 | Capitólio and a boat trip on the lake |
| Days 11–12 | Return to São Paulo, handing back motorcycles |

This sequence brings several experiences into one journey. Paraty offers colonial streets and the coast; Rio brings famous city panoramas; and the roads of Minas Gerais pass through mountain scenery. **Lake Furnas appears towards the end, after several long motorcycle stages.**

The trip belongs to our [motorcycle tours in Brazil](/interests/motorcycle-tours/tours/brazil/). Choosing it solely for the lake makes sense if you also enjoy the ride itself: a considerable share of the 12 days is spent traveling between towns.

## How much time is spent in Capitólio and at Furnas?

On day 9, after sightseeing in Tiradentes, the group rides to Capitólio. The distance for this stage is around 320 km. Accommodation is arranged near the lake after arrival.

**Day 10 is devoted to Capitólio.** The itinerary includes a boat trip on Furnas, views of the canyon walls and an opportunity to swim near waterfalls. There is no long motorcycle transfer that day. After the road stages, this is a full break for exploring the area's natural scenery.

On day 11, the journey continues to São Paulo. A stop is planned in Holambra, known for its flower-growing traditions; this day's road distance is approximately 360 km. Capitólio therefore occupies the evening after arrival and the following day on the water before the group returns towards its starting point.

The Furnas canyons are a well-known geological attraction near Capitólio. They can be seen from the water and land-based viewpoints, but **the confirmed activity on this specific tour is the boat excursion**. Admission to a separate viewpoint should not be treated as included unless the tour's conditions explicitly say so.

## Who will enjoy this motorcycle journey?

The distinctive feature of this program is riding through Brazil on Triumph Big Trail Tiger 900 motorcycles. **Motorcycle rental is for 10 days**, although the entire trip lasts 12 days and 11 nights. Some days are dedicated to sightseeing and more relaxed stops without long rides, including Paraty, Rio and Capitólio.

The itinerary suits travelers who enjoy riding for several consecutive days. Some daily sections reach roughly 350–360 km. Assess the effort based on the longest daily distance, the time allocated for stops and your own riding experience, not simply the total tour duration.

Luggage is transported separately. The program includes a support vehicle for participants who prefer not to ride a motorcycle. **This is not a promise of a private car for each participant every day**: the arrangements and available seats should be checked against the stated support format.

If you would like to see the canyons and waterfalls without a multi-day ride, start by exploring [Capitólio](/brazil/place/capitolio/) and [Lake Furnas](/brazil/place/lake-furnas/) themselves. The current selection of tours visiting the lake is primarily intended for those choosing a longer road journey.

## What is included and what is paid separately?

The trip includes accommodation in 3–4-star hotels with breakfast and twin-bed rooms, excursions, guide services, rental of a Triumph Big Trail Tiger 900 for 10 days, luggage transport and a support vehicle. These are the actual conditions of the [12-day motorcycle tour](/brazil/tour/brazil-motorcycle-tour-12-days/), not standard inclusions for every trip to Capitólio.

International flights, additional meals, personal expenses, road tolls, extra luggage expenses and motorcycle insurance are listed separately. The program requires a **$2000 credit-card deposit** for the Triumph 900. An extra hotel night after returning the motorcycle and an optional visit to Bohemia are also separate expenses.

{{#if catalog.hasComparableUsdPrice}}
The starting price for this journey is {{catalog.minUsdPriceLabel}}. Compare it with the included services, particularly motorcycle rental, support arrangements and insurance conditions.
{{/if}}

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_source_mototur_cherez_braziliyu}}

## When to plan your stop at the lake

Boat trips on Furnas depend on the weather, lake conditions and current safety regulations. The municipality of Capitólio maintains a register of tourist boats, and the natural canyons require particular attention to navigation conditions. The actual boat outing should therefore be coordinated with the conditions in the chosen travel period.

When planning your journey, it makes sense to preserve the day without a long motorcycle ride that is already provided in the itinerary. If you change the program, avoid reducing it to a brief stop between two long riding days: the point of visiting Furnas on this route is to spend time on the water and see the rocky shoreline.

## Frequently asked questions about tours visiting Furnas

### Is Lake Furnas definitely included in the itinerary?

Yes. The 12-day motorcycle tour includes the lake on its main route, with a boat excursion scheduled for day 10. It is not an optional visit.

### Do you have to ride a motorcycle on all 12 days?

No. Motorcycle rental lasts 10 days. The itinerary includes sightseeing and quieter stops without long transfers, including a day in Capitólio. A support vehicle is available for participants who prefer not to ride.

### How many days are spent at the lake?

Participants arrive in Capitólio on day 9, take a boat trip on Furnas on day 10 and return towards São Paulo on day 11. The full day devoted to the lake is day ten.

### Can you replace the boat trip with an independent canyon excursion?

The published itinerary confirms a boat trip. Other ways to visit, including land-based viewpoints, need to be arranged separately and are not automatically included.

### What should you check before choosing the tour?

Compare daily riding distances with your experience, review motorcycle rental and insurance conditions, the deposit and separately paid expenses. The full program is available on the [Brazil motorcycle tour page](/brazil/tour/brazil-motorcycle-tour-12-days/).

## Lençóis Maranhenses: when to see lagoons among the dunes

[Lençóis Maranhenses National Park](/brazil/place/lencois-maranhenses/) in Brazil is famous for an unusual combination: vast expanses of pale sand dunes and freshwater lagoons that fill during the rainy season. In **2024**, the park was inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List as a natural area of exceptional significance.

The main planning question is **how much water will remain between the dunes in your chosen month**. Some travelers want to swim in blue and green lagoons, while others prefer to hike through the sandy landscape and watch the sunset. These aims call for different dates and different lengths of stay.

## How the lagoons form and why the landscape changes

The dunes lie on the Atlantic coast of Maranhão state. During the rainy season, water gathers in depressions between them, creating temporary lakes whose depth and shape change from year to year. When the rains end and the water gradually evaporates, some lagoons become shallow or disappear altogether.

The scenery you see in photographs therefore does not remain the same throughout the year. Even within one season, some lagoons may be full while others are already shallow. **The same depth of water cannot be guaranteed in every named lagoon**, particularly early or late in the season.

According to information published by ICMBio, the park can be visited year-round, while **May through September** is generally the best period to see lagoons filled after the rains. Conditions within these months still depend on actual rainfall, so it is best to finalize the detailed route closer to departure.

| Period | Main consideration |
|---|---|
| Rainy months | Access and rainfall |
| May–September | Water levels in the lagoons |
| Late dry season | How much water remains |

This table describes the general seasonal pattern, not a forecast for any particular year. If swimming in the lagoons is your main goal, travel dates matter more than trying to visit the greatest number of sights in a single day.

## São Luís, Barreirinhas and Atins: where to start

[São Luís](/brazil/place/sao-luis/) is Maranhão's main urban hub and a convenient starting point after arriving by air. However, the national park itself is **outside the city**, and you will need a separate overland transfer to one of its access points.

For a first visit, many travelers choose [Barreirinhas](/brazil/place/barreirinhas/), the base for excursions to the dunes and lagoons. From there, for example, you can plan a trip to [Lagoa Azul](/brazil/place/lagoa-azul-lencois-maranhenses/). The coastal village of [Atins](/brazil/place/atins/) appeals to visitors seeking a quieter seaside stop and a different way of dividing their time outdoors.

Each base involves a different transport plan. Do not assume that every beach, lagoon or village can be reached directly by a regular car. The national park has specific vehicle restrictions, and transfer times vary according to the chosen route, sand conditions and weather.

Decide in advance where you will stay and how many trips into the park you want to make. Constant transfers between bases reduce the time available on the dunes themselves. If you have several days, leave a free window in case of rain or a change in access to the lagoons.

## What happens on a dune excursion?

Typical activities include walking on the sand, stopping at dune-top viewpoints, swimming in lagoons and photographing the landscape. Some routes involve shorter walks, while others require considerably more time on loose sand in exposed areas.

ICMBio recommends using **accredited guides and transport operators**. Unrestricted driving of private motor vehicles within the protected area is prohibited, and visitors must follow guides' instructions and park rules. According to ICMBio's published information, there is no government admission fee simply to enter the national park; **guide and transport services are paid separately** according to the operators' terms.

For a day trip, bring drinking water, a hat, sun protection and a way to protect camera equipment from sand. There is little shade on the open dunes, and prolonged exposure to the sun can be tiring even when the basic route is not technically difficult. Multi-day hikes require specific preparation beyond what you would normally pack for a beach visit.

## How much time to allow and what not to confuse

**One excursion day** provides a first impression of the dunes and one group of lagoons, but cannot cover the entire park. **Two or three days at your chosen base** give you more freedom for different routes, morning or evening outings and weather changes. Multi-day trekking calls for a different level of fitness and separately arranged guiding.

Do not confuse this landscape with a dry desert that has no water. The dunes of Lençóis Maranhenses lie in a tropical coastal zone, and the temporary lagoons form because of rain. It is a natural area with its own ecosystems, not simply a setting for an unrestricted off-road drive in any direction.

For a cultural addition, spend time in [São Luís](/brazil/place/sao-luis/), which has a protected historic center of its own. This combines two quite different experiences in Maranhão—architecture and natural landscapes—without treating them as interchangeable.

## Frequently asked questions about Lençóis Maranhenses

### When are the lagoons usually fullest?

Usually **after the rainy period, roughly from May through September**. The exact conditions in a particular lagoon depend on that year's rainfall.

### Can you visit the park from São Luís in one day?

The park is **outside the city** and requires a separate road transfer. A day trip including the drive may be tiring; consider staying overnight closer to a park access point.

### Is there an admission fee for the national park?

According to ICMBio's information at the time of the source check, **there is no government fee for entry itself**. However, authorized guide and transport services are charged according to the organizers' terms, and the rules may change.

### Can you drive your own car over the dunes?

**No. Private cars cannot drive freely across the dunes.** Organized trips must meet specific requirements for vehicles and authorized personnel.

### Can you swim in the lagoons?

Swimming is one of the main attractions **when the chosen lagoon has water and is accessible**. Safe swimming locations are determined according to current conditions and the guide's instructions.

## Tours visiting Lençóis Maranhenses: how to choose

[Lençóis Maranhenses](/brazil/place/lencois-maranhenses/) is a national park in Maranhão state in northeastern Brazil. Its white sand dunes alternate with freshwater lagoons that fill after rainfall. The park became a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2024. For travelers, the season and the number of days actually spent among the dunes are essential: merely seeing the park's name on an itinerary does not tell you how much time there will be for walks and swimming.

We offer {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}. Some shorter itineraries focus on Lençóis itself, while longer journeys include the park as a final natural destination after exploring other parts of the country. **The best way to compare programs is by their route within Maranhão**, the number of nights in Barreirinhas or Atins and the time reserved for lagoon excursions.

Our separate [Lençóis Maranhenses destination page](/brazil/place/lencois-maranhenses/) explains the park's natural features. Here, the focus is choosing a ready-made tour. You can find other destinations in our [Brazil tours catalog](/brazil/tour/).

## Which itineraries include the national park?

| Program | Main distinction |
|---|---|
| [4 days: Lençóis](/brazil/tour/lencois-maranhenses/) | São Luís, dunes and river |
| [8 days: Pantanal and Bonito](/brazil/tour/pantanal-bonito-lencois-maranhenses-8-days/) | Safari, clear rivers, lagoons |
| [13 days: Rio, Iguazú, Pipa](/multi-country/tour/brazil-rio-iguazu-lencois-natal-pipa-13-days/) | Dunes, Atins and beaches |
| [14 days: Amazing Brazil](/brazil/tour/amazing-brazil/) | Rio, Pantanal, Amazon |
| [17 days: Grand Adventure](/brazil/tour/grand-brazil-adventure-17-days/) | Rio, an island, Iguazú and nature |

These tours vary in duration and logistics. The short itinerary is designed to explore Lençóis Maranhenses itself. The longer routes make sense if you want to combine the dunes with wildlife in the [Pantanal](/brazil/place/pantanal/), the transparent rivers of [Bonito](/brazil/place/bonito/), the Iguazú Falls or the ocean coast.

### 4 days: dunes and river without traveling across all Brazil

The [4-day Lençóis Maranhenses tour](/brazil/tour/lencois-maranhenses/) starts in [São Luís](/brazil/place/sao-luis/). On day two, travelers head to [Barreirinhas](/brazil/place/barreirinhas/), then continue in 4×4 vehicles to the dunes and [Lagoa Azul](/brazil/place/lagoa-azul-lencois-maranhenses/). There is time to swim and watch the sunset.

The following day focuses on the Preguiças River before returning to São Luís. One day is therefore devoted to the sand dunes and lagoons, and the next to the river and coastal settlements. This is a logical choice for those primarily interested in Maranhão who do not want to add flights across the country.

### 8 days: Pantanal, Bonito and Lençóis

The [8-day itinerary](/brazil/tour/pantanal-bonito-lencois-maranhenses-8-days/) connects 3 natural regions. Travelers first watch wildlife in the Pantanal, then visit waterfalls, caves and the clear waters of Bonito. Day 5 includes a flight to São Luís, day 6 a journey to Barreirinhas and the dunes, and day 7 a boat trip along the Preguiças River and return to São Luís.

This option is useful if you want to experience several landscapes but have limited time for a comprehensive tour of Brazil. However, **the dunes and river outing occupy 2 consecutive days**, not several free days in the park.

### 13 days: Lençóis, Atins and a beach finale

The [13-day program](/multi-country/tour/brazil-rio-iguazu-lencois-natal-pipa-13-days/) begins in Rio de Janeiro, visits both sides of the Iguazú Falls and then heads to Maranhão. On day 8, travelers reach Barreirinhas and the lagoons. Day 9 includes the Preguiças River, [Vassouras](/brazil/place/vassouras-lencois-maranhenses/) and arrival in [Atins](/brazil/place/atins/); day 10 brings an excursion to the Atins lagoon and a return to Barreirinhas.

The route then continues via Natal to [Praia de Pipa](/brazil/place/praia-de-pipa/). This suits travelers who want both the dunes and the coast, with several days exploring different sections of Lençóis. Importantly, the visit to the Argentine side of Iguazú is part of the program: the product is listed among multi-country tours even though most of the itinerary is in Brazil.

### 14 and 17 days: the national park as part of a larger journey

The [14-day Amazing Brazil tour](/brazil/tour/amazing-brazil/) connects Rio, the Pantanal, Bonito, Amazonian Manaus, São Luís and Barreirinhas. Lençóis Maranhenses appears towards the end of the route, after the Amazon section. It is a choice for those who want to contrast dunes with rainforest and the country's other natural regions.

The [17-day Grand Adventure](/brazil/tour/grand-brazil-adventure-17-days/) adds Ilha Grande, Iguazú, the Pantanal and Bonito to Rio. On day 14, travelers go from São Luís to Barreirinhas and head out to the dunes and lagoons. Day 15 brings a boat trip on the Preguiças River. Here, the park is one of the final highlights after a long journey through several parts of Brazil.

**The difference between 14 and 17 days is more than duration.** One tour includes an Amazon stage via Manaus; the other includes an island visit and Iguazú. If Lençóis is your principal goal, choose according to the time spent in Maranhão, rather than the total number of travel days.

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_source_lensojs_maranenses,tour_brazil_pantanal_bonito_lencois_8d,tour_brazil_dunes_13d,tour_source_udivitelnaya_braziliya,tour_brazil_adventure_17d}}

## Barreirinhas, Atins and São Luís: how the stops differ

[São Luís](/brazil/place/sao-luis/) is a key transport and cultural hub before visiting the park. Its historic buildings have facades covered with Portuguese azulejo tiles. Ada Tours itineraries include a road transfer from São Luís to Barreirinhas of approximately 3.5–4 hours, depending on the particular route.

[Barreirinhas](/brazil/place/barreirinhas/) is a base for lagoon excursions. From there, 4×4 trips visit the dune fields and boats explore the Preguiças River. [Lagoa Azul](/brazil/place/lagoa-azul-lencois-maranhenses/) features on well-known swimming routes, although the actual lagoons visited can change according to rainfall and sand conditions.

[Atins](/brazil/place/atins/) lies nearer the mouth of the Preguiças River and the ocean. It is included in the 13-day itinerary, which features a night in the village and a separate lagoon outing. **Not every tour of Lençóis Maranhenses visits Atins.** If you want to explore this section, choose a program that names it explicitly.

## When to visit for full lagoons

At Lençóis Maranhenses, water collects between the dunes after the rainy season. The national park can be visited throughout the year, but the scenery varies by month: during drier periods, many temporary lagoons become shallow or disappear.

For trips emphasizing swimming and water-filled lagoons, **May through September is generally the preferred period**, especially the months following the main rains. Actual water levels depend on that year's weather. Before choosing a date, it is more useful to check lagoon conditions and access to the specific routes included in your tour than only the general forecast for São Luís.

The park contains both temporary and permanent lagoons. Their shape, depth and even position relative to routes change with wind and rainfall. A lagoon's fixed name does not guarantee the same scenery in every month.

## How dune excursions work

Trips from Barreirinhas use special off-road vehicles and approved routes. Park administrator ICMBio requires authorized drivers and guides to accompany visitors, and vehicles must have permission to operate. Walks take place on soft sand in exposed sunny areas, so comfortable shoes, sun protection and drinking water are important.

A boat trip on the Preguiças River offers another perspective: mangrove-lined banks, villages, small sandy stretches, a lighthouse and coastal views replace the lines of dunes. Some itineraries include the outing, while the stops may differ in others. Always check the excursion details in the specific program.

If you mainly enjoy active exploration, see our [adventure tours in Brazil](/interests/adventure/tours/brazil/). Travelers who want to add wildlife watching can explore the [nature and wildlife itinerary selection](/interests/wildlife/tours/brazil/).

## What to compare in prices and transfers

A short trip and a large combined tour include fundamentally different services. Total duration does not tell you whether domestic flights, private transport, an English-speaking guide or extra excursions are included. For example, domestic flights are paid separately on the 17-day program, and some transfers are shared.

{{#if catalog.hasComparableUsdPrice}}
The lowest comparable tour price in this selection is {{catalog.minUsdPriceLabel}}. Use it as a guide when choosing a program, not as the price of identical services across all options.
{{/if}}

For a practical comparison, consider 3 points: **the number of days in the park itself, which transfers are included and the language of your guide**. Then decide whether you want a route through the Pantanal, Bonito, Amazon or a beach region. The more regions the trip covers, the more important it is to allow sufficient time for flights and transfers between them.

## Frequently asked questions about tours to Lençóis Maranhenses

### Which tour is best if I only want dunes and lagoons?

Start with the [4-day Lençóis Maranhenses program](/brazil/tour/lencois-maranhenses/). It concentrates on São Luís, Barreirinhas, lagoon visits and the Preguiças River, without a long route through other states.

### Which itineraries include Atins?

Atins is confirmed on the [13-day journey through Rio, Iguazú, Lençóis and Pipa](/multi-country/tour/brazil-rio-iguazu-lencois-natal-pipa-13-days/). It includes stops at Vassouras, arrival in Atins and a separate lagoon outing before returning to Barreirinhas.

### Can you combine Lençóis with the Pantanal and Bonito?

Yes. Both appear, for example, in the [8-day program](/brazil/tour/pantanal-bonito-lencois-maranhenses-8-days/) and the [17-day Grand Adventure](/brazil/tour/grand-brazil-adventure-17-days/). The difference is the additional geography and overall trip duration.

### When are the lagoons usually fullest?

Most commonly from May through September, following the rains. Exact conditions depend on the year's precipitation; some lagoons are seasonal and gradually dry out.

### Do you have to book a separate lagoon excursion?

The listed itineraries include visits to the dunes, but the exact excursions and charged services differ. Only accredited operators may run park trips. Compare the excursion list with the [specific tour description](/brazil/tour/lencois-maranhenses/), particularly if you want to alter your route on site.

  Maceió is the capital of Brazil's Alagoas state and a convenient starting point for holidays on the Atlantic coast. The city is known for Pajuçara, Ponta Verde and Jatiúca beaches, its waterfront promenade and natural tidal pools that are best visited at low tide. Your choice of neighborhood and travel dates shapes the experience.
---

## Maceió: what to expect on the Alagoas coast

Maceió lies on the Atlantic coast of northeastern [Brazil](/brazil/). It is the capital of Alagoas state, attracting travelers who want to combine city life with the sea. Some beachfront neighborhoods have hotels, restaurants and a long promenade; farther away are coastal areas reached on separate day trips.

For a first trip to Maceió, it helps to distinguish two approaches. You can stay near the urban waterfront and combine walks, swimming and outings to natural pools. Alternatively, use Maceió as a transport hub and stay on a more remote stretch of the Alagoas coast. The actual activities depend on your specific tour and accommodation.

## Main city beaches: Pajuçara, Ponta Verde and Jatiúca

### Pajuçara and the natural pools

Pajuçara Beach is known for natural tidal pools that form among offshore reefs at low tide. Trips to these pools are organized on traditional sailing rafts called *jangadas*. The difference between high and low tide determines when the reefs are visible and how outings can be arranged.

Do not choose your departure time solely by the hour shown on a clock. Tides shift from one day to another, and sea conditions can affect whether the trip is possible. Before booking, check the tide forecast and confirm conditions with the operator.

### Ponta Verde and the waterfront promenade

Ponta Verde is one of the city's best-known coastal areas. Palm trees, cafes and walking areas line the beach. The landscape changes noticeably at low tide, when sections of reefs and sand become exposed. It is a pleasant place for a seaside stroll even if the swimming conditions are different from what you expected.

### Jatiúca: a different type of sea

Jatiúca continues the series of city beaches, but its waves may differ from the more sheltered reef areas of Pajuçara. The three beaches should not all be described as equally calm or safe for swimming. When planning a beach day, follow lifeguard warnings, actual wave conditions and local advice.

For a wider comparison of seaside destinations, visit our [beach holidays section](/interests/beach-holidays/). It covers different countries and resorts, whereas Maceió is a specific city on the Alagoas coast.

## What to see beyond the beach

Maceió is interesting as a city in its own right. In the Jaraguá district, buildings associated with the city's trading history remain; markets and craft shops introduce visitors to locally made goods. A stroll along the waterfront is pleasant towards evening when the heat feels less intense.

Alagoas cuisine is closely connected with the sea: fish, shrimp and dishes prepared with regional ingredients are common. Restaurant choices and meal arrangements depend on your own plans or the specific tour. Trying local cuisine does not automatically mean a gastronomic excursion is included.

Other coastal areas lie beyond the city beaches. Some travelers take a separate trip to beaches and lagoons south of Maceió, while others explore the northern part of the state. Such outings take extra time: straight-line distances on a map may differ significantly from the actual road journey.

## When to visit Maceió and how to account for tides

The Atlantic coast of northeastern Brazil is warm throughout the year, but rainfall, cloud cover and sea conditions vary with the seasons. Travel planning therefore involves two separate considerations: the overall weather season and **the tide on the particular day** when you want to visit the reef pools.

For a walk along the coast, a few cloudy hours rarely spoil the experience. A trip to the reefs, however, requires suitable water levels and safe sea conditions. If that outing is your main goal, allow for the possibility of moving it to another morning or day. The operator determines the departure time and whether the trip can go ahead.

Brazil's beach resorts have different climates. Travelers combining Maceió with distant parts of the country need to account for domestic flights and changing weather. The easiest way to compare possible destinations is through our [Brazil tours](/brazil/tour/), checking the geography and duration.

## Choosing where to stay and what kind of trip to take

If you want to stay by the city waterfront, look at accommodation near Pajuçara, Ponta Verde or Jatiúca, although the specific hotel depends on your budget and available itinerary. For a quieter holiday away from urban traffic, consider other areas along the Alagoas coast and allow time for transport.
